 Judgment
1.
The insurer is in appeal challenging the negligence attributed to the rider of the vehicle which it had insured.

Sathisha vs Basavaraju @ Basavarajanaika on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48129231/
3 2.
The claimant is in appeal contending that the denial of any sum towards loss of amenities by the Tribunal was incorrect.
It is also contended that the sum awarded toward pain and suffering is on the lower side.

3. As far as the negligence is concerned, the rider of the offending vehicle himself has admitted in his cross- examination that the claimant suddenly took a right turn and he hit the claimant from behind.
This indicates that the collision was due to the improper driving of the rider of the insured vehicle.

4. It is also pertinent to state here that a charge sheet has been laid against the rider of the offending vehicle and hence, prima-facie even according to the Police, the negligence was attributable to the rider of the insured vehicle.
Learned counsel however contends that the rider of the offending vehicle had filed a private complaint and therefore, no credence can be given to the charge sheet.
Merely because a private complaint is fled, that would not indicate that the rider of the offending vehicle was negligent.

5. Having regard to the manner in which the accident occurred and the evidence of the driver himself, it is clear that the Tribunal was justified in holding that the rider of the insured vehicle was responsible for the accident.
Thus, there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer and the same is therefore dismissed.

6. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 90,000
2 . Medical expenses 48,747  Loss of income during the laid
3. 20,000 up period and attendant charges 4. Conveyance, food, nourishment 40,000 Total 1,98,747 7
. In my view, the Tribunal has only committed an error in not awarding any sum towards loss of amenities.

Sathisha vs Basavaraju @ Basavarajanaika on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48129231/
4 8.
The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered 32.5% disability to the whole body and the injury suffered includes the head injury.

In that view of the matter, it would be appropriated to award a sum of Rs.90,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
9.
The compensation awarded under the other heads are just and proper and the same do not call for modification and hence confirmed.

10. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
 As As  awarded awarded  Sl. Compensation under  by the by this
No . different
Heads  Tribunal Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)

1. Pain and sufferings 90,000 90,000  2. Medical expenses 48,747 48,747  Loss of income during  3. the laid up period and 20,000 20,000  attendant charges  Conveyance, food,
 4. 40,000 40,000  nourishment  7. Loss of amenities in life 0 90,000
11 . Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.2,88,747/- as against Rs.1,98,747/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
13. The interest awarded at 7% by the Tribunal is scale down to 6%.
14. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.

5 15.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
16. The appeal of the claimant is accordingly allowed in part.
